proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(X_Y(a)=(a,Y_Y^{\mathrm{obs}}(a))\).  By \(\texttt{def:pair-invariance-group}\), every \(g\in G_J\) permutes pairs and possibly exchanges the two labels inside each pair.  Hence it preserves each armwise discordance count \(D_a\), the binary class \(\Theta_{J,s}\) from \(\texttt{ass:binary-outcome-support}\) and \(\texttt{ass:armwise-discordance-budget}\), and the unit-weighted contrast \(\tau\).  It also satisfies the observation equivariance identity
\[
 g^{-1}X_Y(gb)=X_{g^{-1}Y}(b).
\]

Fix an admissible pair \((Q,\delta)\).  Define
\[
 \overline Q(a)=\frac1{|G_J|}\sum_{g\in G_J}Q(g^{-1}a).
\]
The law \(\overline Q\) is chosen before outcomes and is outcome-independent by \(\texttt{ass:design-exogeneity}\), so it belongs to \(\mathfrak Q_{J,s}\).  If \(\overline Q(a)>0\), set
\[
 w_g(a)=\frac{Q(g^{-1}a)}{\sum_{u\in G_J}Q(u^{-1}a)},
 \qquad
 \overline\delta(a,y)=\sum_{g\in G_J}w_g(a)\delta(g^{-1}a,g^{-1}y),
\]
and set \(\overline\delta(a,y)=0\) when \(\overline Q(a)=0\).  The weights use only the observed assignment and the known design.  Thus \(\overline\delta\) is measurable from \((A,Y^{\mathrm{obs}},\mathcal P_J)\), and it lies in \([-1,1]\) because it is a convex combination of clipped estimators.

Equivalently, draw \(g\) uniformly from \(G_J\), draw \(b\sim Q\), and report the relabelled assignment \(a=gb\).  Conditional on \(a\), the distribution of \(g\) is \(w_g(a)\).  Conditional Jensen inequality for squared loss, observation equivariance, and \(\tau(g^{-1}Y)=\tau(Y)\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal R_{J,s}(\overline Q,\overline\delta;Y)
 &\le \frac1{|G_J|}\sum_{g\in G_J}
 \mathcal R_{J,s}(Q,\delta;g^{-1}Y)\\
 &\le \sup_{Y'\in\Theta_{J,s}}\mathcal R_{J,s}(Q,\delta;Y').
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore restriction to invariant procedures does not change the minimax value.

The assignment orbits of this action are exactly the triples \(n=(n_{00},n_{11},n_{\mathrm m})\in\mathcal N_J\), and an invariant assignment law is uniform inside each orbit and is specified by \(q\).  A schedule orbit is exactly a histogram \(h\in\mathcal H_{J,s}\) of the ten unordered pair types, and its target is \(\tau_h\).  Because each local observed unit records both \(A_{jr}\) and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{jr}\), an observation orbit is exactly a histogram \(o\in\mathcal O_J\); in particular it retains the joint assignment--outcome pair type.  Hence an invariant estimator is specified by the values \(\eta_{no}\) on compatible orbit cells.

We next verify the kernel.  Choose a list \(t_1,\ldots,t_J\) containing \(h_t\) copies of every \(t\in\mathcal T\).  Let \(M_0(0,0)=1\), with every other value zero, and recursively define
\[
 M_{k+1}(n,o)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}}
 M_k\!\left(n-e_{\nu(a)},o-e_{\omega(t_{k+1},a)}\right),
\]
where a term with a negative coordinate is zero.  Induction on \(k\) shows that \(M_k(n,o)\) is the number of local assignment strings for the first \(k\) pairs with assignment mark \(n\) and observed-pair mark \(o\).  The induction starts from the empty string; appending \(a\) gives exactly the displayed recurrence.  Thus
\[
 M_J(n,o)=
 [x_{00}^{n_{00}}x_{11}^{n_{11}}x_{\mathrm m}^{n_{\mathrm m}}z^o]F_h(x,z).
\]
There are
\[
 C_n=\frac{J!2^{n_{\mathrm m}}}{n_{00}!n_{11}!n_{\mathrm m}!}
\]
labelled assignments in orbit \(n\).  Consequently
\[
 K_{hno}=\frac{M_J(n,o)}{C_n},
 \qquad
 \sum_{o\in\mathcal O_J}K_{hno}=1,
\]
which proves that \(K\) is the conditional observation law rather than merely defining it to be one.

The cardinalities satisfy
\[
 |\mathcal N_J|={J+2\choose2},\qquad
 |\mathcal H_{J,s}|\le {J+9\choose9},\qquad
 |\mathcal O_J|={J+9\choose9}.
\]
Therefore the full rectangular array has at most
\[
 {J+2\choose2}{J+9\choose9}^{\!2}=O(J^{20})
\]
entries.  Since \(0\le M_J(n,o)\le4^J\) and \(1\le C_n\le4^J\), the numerator and denominator of every reduced rational \(K_{hno}\) have \(O(J)\) bits.  The recurrence uses integer additions and computes all coefficients exactly.

It remains to derive the finite game and its dual.  Put \(t_{no}=q_n\eta_{no}\) and define the compact convex perspective set
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{pr}}=
 \left\{(q,t):q_n\ge0,\ \sum_nq_n=1,\ -q_n\le t_{no}\le q_n
 \text{ for all }n,o\right\}.
\]
For \(q_n>0\), write
\[
 \psi_{hno}(q_n,t_{no})
 =K_{hno}\frac{(t_{no}-q_n\tau_h)^2}{q_n},
\]
and set \(\psi_{hno}(0,0)=0\).  This is the closed perspective of a convex quadratic.  Moreover, on the displayed wedge,
\[
 0\le \psi_{hno}(q_n,t_{no})
 =q_nK_{hno}(t_{no}/q_n-\tau_h)^2
 \le4K_{hno}q_n,
\]
so it is continuous also at \(q_n=0\).  Thus
\[
 \Phi((q,t),\pi)=\sum_h\pi_h\sum_{n,o}\psi_{hno}(q_n,t_{no})
\]
is continuous and convex in \((q,t)\), and affine, hence concave, in \(\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal H_{J,s})\).  Applying \(\texttt{lem:sion-minimax}\) on the two compact convex sets yields
\[
 \min_{(q,t)\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{pr}}}\max_{\pi}\Phi((q,t),\pi)
 =\max_{\pi}\min_{(q,t)\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{pr}}}\Phi((q,t),\pi),
\]
with both extrema attained.  The left maximum over \(\pi\) is the maximum over \(h\), so it is exactly the invariant minimax game and hence, by symmetrization, \(R^*(J,s)\).

For fixed \(\pi\), define
\[
 d_{no}(\pi)=\sum_h\pi_hK_{hno}\tau_h^2.
\]
The contribution of cell \((n,o)\) to \(\Phi\) is
\[
 a_{no}(\pi)\frac{t_{no}^2}{q_n}-2c_{no}(\pi)t_{no}+q_nd_{no}(\pi).
\]
If \(a_{no}(\pi)>0\), completing the square gives the unique minimizing ratio
\[
 \frac{t_{no}}{q_n}=\frac{c_{no}(\pi)}{a_{no}(\pi)}.
\]
This ratio is a conditional average of \(\tau_h\in[-1,1]\), so it satisfies the clipping constraint.  If \(a_{no}(\pi)=0\), nonnegativity of \(\pi_hK_{hno}\) implies \(c_{no}(\pi)=d_{no}(\pi)=0\), and the cell contributes zero at its minimum.  Finally, row normalization gives
\[
 \sum_o d_{no}(\pi)=\sum_h\pi_h\tau_h^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \min_t\Phi((q,t),\pi)
 =\sum_nq_n\left\{\sum_h\pi_h\tau_h^2-
 \sum_{o:a_{no}(\pi)>0}\frac{c_{no}(\pi)^2}{a_{no}(\pi)}\right\}
 =\sum_nq_nB_n(\pi).
\]
Minimizing this linear expression over \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J)\) gives \(\min_nB_n(\pi)\).  We have proved
\[
 R^*(J,s)=\min_{q,\eta}\max_h\mathcal R_h(q,\eta)
 =\max_{\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal H_{J,s})}\min_{n\in\mathcal N_J}B_n(\pi).
\]

For the contact certificate, first suppose \(q\in\mathcal Q^*(J,s)\).  Choose an attaining invariant estimator \(\eta\), choose an attaining dual prior \(\pi\), and put \(v=R^*(J,s)\).  Primal and dual feasibility give
\[
 \mathcal R_h(q,\eta)\le v\quad\text{for every }h,
 \qquad
 B_n(\pi)\ge v\quad\text{for every }n.
\]
Conversely, if these inequalities hold for some \((q,\eta,\pi,v)\), weak duality and the equality just proved give
\[
 R^*(J,s)le\max_h\mathcal R_h(q,\eta)le v
 \le\min_nB_n(\pi)\le R^*(J,s).
\]
Every inequality is therefore an equality, and \(q\in\mathcal Q^*(J,s)\).  Fixing \(q=q^{\mathrm{pair}}\) or \(q=q^{\mathrm{Ber}}\) yields the two membership tests.  Adding the variable \(0\le\lambda\le1\) and the constraint \(q=\lambda q^{\mathrm{pair}}+(1-\lambda)q^{\mathrm{Ber}}\) tests intersection with \(\mathcal C_J\); infeasibility certifies essential noncanonicality.  The optimal subset of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{pr}}\) is compact and convex, and its projection onto the \(q\)-coordinates is exactly \(\mathcal Q^*(J,s)\).  This projection is a singleton if and only if, for every \(n\), the minimum and maximum of \(q_n\) over it agree.  These coordinate optimizations give the asserted uniqueness certificate.

Use the deterministic ordering in \(\texttt{def:j2-rational-certificate}\), with indices beginning at zero.  The six assignment-orbit sizes are
\[
 (C_n)_n=(4,4,1,4,2,1),
\]
and the Bernoulli orbit masses are
\[
 (q_n^{\mathrm{Ber}})_n=(1/4,1/4,1/16,1/4,1/8,1/16).
\]
All displayed coordinates of \(q^{\mathrm U}\), \(\pi^{\mathrm U}\), and \(\pi^{\mathrm H}\) are nonnegative, and direct integer summation gives respectively \(100\), \(10^8\), and \(10^8\); hence they are probability vectors.  If
\[
 q^{\mathrm U}=\lambda q^{\mathrm{pair}}+(1-\lambda)q^{\mathrm{Ber}},
\]
then the last coordinate gives \((1-\lambda)/16=1/100\), or \(1-\lambda=4/25\).  The second coordinate would then be \((1-\lambda)/4=1/25\), but the second coordinate of \(q^{\mathrm U}\) is \(3/10\).  Thus \(q^{\mathrm U}\notin\mathcal C_2\).

We now perform the exact kernel check and record a nondegeneracy witness.  Histogram \(20\) consists of local schedule types \(3\) and \(7\), namely
\[
 t_3=\{(0,0),(1,1)\},
 \qquad
 t_7=\{(1,0),(1,0)\},
 \qquad
 h^{20}=e_{t_3}+e_{t_7}.
\]
It is feasible because each arm is discordant in exactly one pair, and
\[
 \tau_{h^{20}}=\frac{0+(-2)}4=-\frac12.
\]
The singleton region \(\{h^{20}\}\) has strictly positive mass under both certificate priors:
\[
 \pi^{\mathrm U}_{20}=\frac{16328392}{10^8}
 =\frac{2041049}{12500000}>0,
 \qquad
 \pi^{\mathrm H}_{20}=\frac{15653588}{10^8}
 =\frac{3913397}{25000000}>0.
\]

Uniformity inside assignment orbits and the displayed orbit sizes give, in the fixed six-orbit order,
\[
 \left(\frac{q_n^{\mathrm U}}{C_n}\right)_n
 =\left(\frac9{100},\frac3{40},\frac1{100},
 \frac3{40},\frac1{100},\frac1{100}\right).
\]
Thus every one of the \(16\) labelled assignments has probability at least \(1/100\).  Applying the coefficient recurrence of Theorem 1 to the \(16\) local assignment strings for \(h^{20}\) gives twelve positive \((n,o)\) cells and the complete multisets
\[
 \{K_{20,no}:K_{20,no}>0\}
 =\{1^{(2)},(1/2)^{(6)},(1/4)^{(4)}\},
\]
\[
 \{q_n^{\mathrm U}K_{20,no}:K_{20,no}>0\}
 =\{(9/50)^{(2)},(3/20)^{(2)},(3/40)^{(4)},(1/100)^{(4)}\},
\]
where exponents denote multiplicities.  The second multiset sums to one and proves the exact positive observation-orbit support bound
\[
 \min_{(n,o):K_{20,no}>0}q_n^{\mathrm U}K_{20,no}=\frac1{100}.
\]

For two explicit failure-driving cells, index the ten observed-pair types lexicographically and set
\[
 v_3=\{(0,0),(1,1)\},\qquad
 v_5=\{(0,1),(1,0)\},
\]
where each ordered pair is \((A,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Put
\[
 o^{(1)}=e_{v_3}+e_{v_5},\qquad o^{(2)}=2e_{v_5},
 \qquad n^{\mathrm m}=(0,0,2).
\]
The same recurrence, followed by the finite sums defining \(a\) and \(c\), gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
 o & K_{20,n^{\mathrm m},o}&a_{n^{\mathrm m}o}(\pi^{\mathrm U})
 &c_{n^{\mathrm m}o}(\pi^{\mathrm U})&\eta^{\mathrm U}_{n^{\mathrm m}o}\\ \hline
 o^{(1)}&1/2&6531357/40000000&1/400000000&1/65313570\\
 o^{(2)}&1/2&17288147/100000000&-13206049/100000000&-455381/596143
\end{array}
\]
Every denominator is positive.  Since \(q_{n^{\mathrm m}}^{\mathrm U}=36/100\), each cell has probability \(9/50\) under \(q^{\mathrm U}K_{20}\).  Their separate contributions to the risk at \(h^{20}\) are
\[
 \frac9{50}\left(\frac1{65313570}+\frac12\right)^2
 =\frac{266616417962449}{5924808925201250}>0,
\]
and
\[
 \frac9{50}\left(-\frac{455381}{596143}+\frac12\right)^2
 =\frac{890866036449}{71077295289800}>0.
\]
They also prove that the posterior-mean estimator is nonconstant on the observable experiment.  Indeed, for any finite distribution with cell probabilities \(p_i\) and values \(z_i\),
\(
 \operatorname{Var}(Z)=\sum_{i<j}p_ip_j(z_i-z_j)^2
\).
Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{q^{\mathrm U}K_{20}}(\eta^{\mathrm U}_{NO})
 \ge \frac{81}{2500}
 \left(\frac{29742559416313}{38936227560510}\right)^2>0.
\]
This establishes exact design support, positive prior mass, multiple positive risk cells, and nonzero observable estimator variance at the active histogram.

For completeness, evaluating
\[
 \mathcal R_h(q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})
 =\sum_{n,o}q_n^{\mathrm U}\frac{M_h(n,o)}{C_n}
 \left\{\frac{c_{no}(\pi^{\mathrm U})}{a_{no}(\pi^{\mathrm U})}-\tau_h\right\}^2,
\]
with zero on cells for which \(a_{no}(\pi^{\mathrm U})=0\), over all \(38\) feasible histograms gives
\[
 \max_{h\in\mathcal H_{2,1}}\mathcal R_h(q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})
 =\mathcal R_{h^{20}}(q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})
 =\frac{3850693539551962000276103702569949405421799518612146614194263925096941}
 {42480492487647577202373742417068406183238423509974554343379909221067500}.
\]
Exact subtraction yields
\[
 \frac{9065}{100000}-\mathcal R_{h^{20}}(q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})
 =\frac{1304835626326984952608380298412920710108580536373896264998766342623}
 {339843939901180617618989939336547249465907388079796434747039273768540000}>0.
\]

The same coefficient table and \(\texttt{def:conditional-bayes-risk}\) give
\[
 B_{(0,0,2)}(\pi^{\mathrm H})
 =\frac{1120490298829500754077}{12309527381808500000000},
\]
and
\[
 \sum_{n\in\mathcal N_2}q_n^{\mathrm{Ber}}B_n(\pi^{\mathrm H})
 =\frac{1760496146710770175939617592960855471947446378734932636964736609}
 {19340529328385758315873504820452091980056895966176036468000000000}.
\]
Their respective exact excesses over \(9102/100000\) are
\[
 \frac{77116537291084077}{12309527381808500000000}>0
\]
and
\[
 \frac{121167241098454028811184203306059922667707893589797647376609}
 {19340529328385758315873504820452091980056895966176036468000000000}>0.
\]

Finally, consider only the paper-defined endpoint-mixture workflow
\[
 q_\lambda=\lambda q^{\mathrm{pair}}+(1-\lambda)q^{\mathrm{Ber}},
 \qquad 0\le\lambda\le1,
\]
while allowing its estimator to be reoptimized over all measurable clipped rules.  This is an internal benchmark; no cited paper is asserted to advocate this mixture.  For every \(\eta\), maximum risk dominates Bayes risk under \(\pi^{\mathrm H}\), and the cellwise posterior-mean calculation in Theorem 1 gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \max_h\mathcal R_h(q_\lambda,\eta)
 &\ge \inf_{\eta'}\sum_h\pi_h^{\mathrm H}
 \mathcal R_h(q_\lambda,\eta')\\
 &=\lambda B_{(0,0,2)}(\pi^{\mathrm H})
 +(1-\lambda)\sum_nq_n^{\mathrm{Ber}}B_n(\pi^{\mathrm H})\\
 &>\frac{9102}{100000}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The two endpoint excesses displayed above have a strictly positive minimum, so the strict inequality remains uniform after taking the infimum over \(\lambda\) and \(\eta\).  On the other hand, the unrestricted minimax risk is at most the certified risk of \((q^{\mathrm U},\eta^{\mathrm U})\), which is below \(9065/100000\).  Therefore \(\mathcal Q^*(2,1)\cap\mathcal C_2=\varnothing\), and the all-estimator gap is strictly larger than
\[
 \frac{9102-9065}{100000}=\frac{37}{100000}.
\]

Order the assignment orbits as \((0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1),(2,0)\), where the omitted coordinate is \(n_{\mathrm m}=2-n_{00}-n_{11}\), and set
\[
 q^{\mathrm U}=\frac1{100}(36,30,1,30,2,1).
\]
In the stated order on \(\mathcal H_{2,1}\), set
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \pi^{\mathrm U}=10^{-8}(&1015984,0,0,11868045,5323822,0,0,5323822,0,2031967,
 0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,16328393,16328392,11868045,9123951,0,0,0,0,5323822,
 0,0,0,0,0,9123951,0,5323822,0,1015984),
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \pi^{\mathrm H}=10^{-8}(&1674027,0,0,10977951,4888329,0,0,4888329,0,3348054,
 0,1407928,0,0,0,0,1407928,0,0,15653588,15653588,10977951,7427893,0,1407928,
 0,0,4888329,0,0,0,0,0,7427893,1407928,4888329,0,1674027).

For every orbit cell \((n,o)\), compute
\[
 a_{no}(\pi^{\mathrm U})=\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_{2,1}}\pi_h^{\mathrm U}K_{hno},
 \qquad

and define

Together with the coefficient definition of \(K\) and the displayed formula for \(\tau_h\), these coordinates specify every rational quantity in the \(J=2,s=1\) upper and canonical-segment lower certificates without an external table.

Under design unbiasedness for bounded finite-population totals, the minimax bound is attained if and only if inclusion indicators are pairwise independent.

prose_updates.tldr: Known pairs are useful when their two units would respond similarly under each arm, but that two-arm similarity is latent. The integer \(s\) is therefore an analyst-selected sensitivity bound, and for every value the project jointly optimizes over all outcome-independent assignment laws and all measurable clipped SATE estimators. A pair-preserving symmetry reduction yields an exact finite conic game, a polynomial-size rational kernel, and dual certificates for the entire invariant optimal-design correspondence; an exact, nondegenerate \(J=2,s=1\) witness rules out the paper-defined paired--Bernoulli mixture workflow. The unrestricted all-design/all-estimator orbit-game layer and the \(J^{-4/3}\) second-order scale overlap with the accepted internal \texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier\_v1} artifact. The present contribution is instead localized to the known-pair wreath-product action, the hard armwise-discordance subclass, joint assignment--observation pair histograms, and the exact projected optimal-design correspondence; neither a global extension nor priority over that artifact is claimed. The sensitivity frontier satisfies \(J R^*(J,s_J)\to\min\{\rho,1/2\}\), while exact finite-minimizer selection on the flat first-order face remains the open \(J^{2/3}\)-critical, \(J^{-4/3}\)-residual problem.

project_justification.gap: The accepted internal \texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier\_v1} artifact already supplies an unrestricted all-design/all-estimator binary response-type orbit game and establishes \(n^{-4/3}\) second-order scaling, so neither generic orbit minimax nor that scale alone is a gap. Published endpoint results also cover unrestricted binary schedules and a larger unrestricted bounded-interval class. What remains untreated is the intermediate fixed-population class indexed by a latent armwise pair-discordance cap, with a pair-preserving rather than full-unit symmetry, while jointly choosing every assignment law and every measurable estimator and projecting the full contact system onto exact optimal assignment laws. The superpopulation half-treatment and fixed-design linear-estimator comparators remain non-nested with this problem.
project_justification.niche: The known-pair wreath-product action and hard discordance cap break the full unit-permutation geometry used by the neighboring unrestricted artifact. Schedule states are ten-type unordered pair histograms, and the reduced data must retain joint assignment-marked observed-pair histograms. This produces a nontransitive finite experiment whose exact projected design correspondence and interior-budget selection behavior are not consequences of the unrestricted \(2^K\)-response-type game.
project_justification.fill: For each selected \(s\), the project supplies the pair-orbit kernel, the primal game and matching least-favourable-prior dual, an if-and-only-if contact certificate for the projected invariant optimal-design correspondence, exact canonicality and uniqueness tests, and a strict rational \(J=2,s=1\) separation with full assignment support, positive active-prior mass, two explicit positive-risk observation cells, and nonzero posterior-estimator variance. It also proves the sharp first-order phase transition and exact inversion, while formulating but not solving the residual \(J^{4/3}\)-scaled epi-limit and exact-minimizer contact problem. These are adjacent, non-nested contributions, not a claim of global extension or priority over the accepted unrestricted artifact.

prose_updates.related_work: The closest internal comparison is the accepted artifact \texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier\_v1}. Its exact-response-type theorem and the present Theorem 1 overlap at the abstract layer where arbitrary outcome-independent designs and arbitrary measurable estimators are symmetrized into a finite binary orbit game with a least-favourable-prior saddle. Its first-order and second-order theorems also make the unrestricted \(n^{-1}\) leading risk and \(n^{-4/3}\) residual scale shared territory. The constructions are nevertheless non-nested: that artifact uses the full unit-permutation group and complete \(2^K\)-response-type histograms for unrestricted fixed-\(K\) contrasts, whereas this paper uses the known-pair action \(\mathfrak S_J\ltimes(\mathfrak S_2)^J\), a hard two-arm armwise-discordance subclass, ten-type latent pair histograms, joint assignment-marked observed-pair histograms, and an exact projection of the procedure contact set onto \(\mathcal Q^*(J,s)\). No global-extension or priority claim is made in either direction. Bai2023WhyRandomize supplies the general averaging template, and Kallus2021Optimality shows that structured fixed-estimator criteria may favor mixed designs; neither supplies this hard-budget all-estimator projected face.
